meta.title: mahina trace
meta.description: mahina tier-1a trace IR wire format (Phase 5b). The on-disk form of a committed, cached Trace (src/trace.zig). Canonical source; the Zig encoder/decoder under src/gen/ is generated from this by tools/regen-trace-schema.sh and vendored. Consumer: the time-travel visualiser (Phase 7).

ConstString.description: A heap string constant: the raw bytes (mahina strings are byte strings, not necessarily UTF-8).

ConstValue.description: A trace constant. `tag` mirrors mahina's Value.Tag enum (nil=0, boolean=1, int=2, float=3, heap_ref=4). A heap_ref const is always a string (tables/closures are never compile-time constants).

IrInstr.description: One SSA instruction: op, two operand refs, aux immediate, observed type, snapshot index.

Trace.description: A committed, cached trace. The anchor is a stable proto id (assigned at compile time) plus the loop-header pc; the in-memory *const Proto pointer is never serialized. `peeled` (doc 39, wire v3): 1 when the trace was committed from a type-stabilizing peel — its preheader run-once region is a REAL tier-0 iteration, so the first back-edge completes two iterations and a zero-completion deopt replays from the entry state. Semantic, not inferable from the marker (an LICM preheader completes zero iterations). `id` (doc 61 §7.1, wire v5): the trace's stable `Trace.id`, never reused; execution logs join to their trace by it.

TraceFile.description: The top-level artifact: a version word followed by the whole trace cache. The richer recording header (hash seed, FP mode, env snapshot) belongs with effect-recording and is deferred to a later phase.

HeapRef.description: A reference to a heap object by its stable GcHeader.id (src/gc.zig). Every inter-object edge in a snapshot is one of these — never a pointer (an address would leak ASLR and break deterministic replay; docs/design/02-determinism.md).

SnapValue.description: A live runtime Value on the wire (src/value.zig). `tag` mirrors mahina's Value.Tag enum (nil=0, boolean=1, int=2, float=3, heap_ref=4) — the same ordinals as ConstValue. Unlike a trace ConstValue, a heap_ref here may reference ANY heap object (table/closure/string/...), carried as the referenced object's id (HeapRef).

TableEntry.description: One key/value pair from a table's hash part. Array-part entries are stored positionally in HeapTable.array; everything else lands here.

HeapString.description: A heap string object's raw bytes (mahina strings are byte strings, not necessarily UTF-8). Interned at restore.

HeapTable.description: A table object: the dense array part (keys 0..asize-1, positionally — entry i IS logical key i, slot-0 hole included in-band; doc 18) plus the hash part (every other key; an array-covered integer key in the hash is invalid and rejected at restore). Edges are SnapValue heap_refs. metatable_id is the table's metatable as a 1-based optional id (header.id + 1), or 0 when it has none — id 0 IS a live object (the first allocation gets id 0), so a bare id cannot be the none sentinel.

HeapClosure.description: A closure: a stable proto id (rebound from the program image at restore, never serialized inline — same stance as a trace anchor) plus the ids of its captured upvalue cells.

HeapUpvalue.description: A captured-variable cell. closed=1: `value` is the held value. closed=0 (open): `value` is the CURRENT contents of the stack slot at capture; restore re-derives the live slot from the saved stack window + Keyframe.open_upvalues (F2b).

HeapNative.description: A native (host/builtin) function, identified by name. Rebound to the installed base library by name at restore (the function pointer is meaningless on disk), so only the name is serialized.

HeapObject.description: One heap object in a snapshot, tagged by `obj_type` (mirrors object.ObjectType: string=0, table=1, function=2, native=3, upvalue=4). `id` is the object's stable GcHeader.id and the key every HeapRef points at. typed_array(5)/host(6) have no variant yet — emitting one is a serializer bug (UnsupportedObject), not a silent drop.

OpenUpvalueRef.description: An open upvalue's binding: the absolute stack index its cell points at, and the cell's object id. Lets restore re-point the cell into the rebuilt stack window. F2a (final-state capture) emits none; load-bearing in F2b.

FrameRef.description: One active call frame, with the execution cursor needed to RESUME it mid-execution (F2c): the executing closure's id, the resumable program counter, the register-window base on the shared stack, the return-wiring (where this frame's results land in its parent, and how many the parent wants), and the live vararg cursor. Windows stack contiguously: frames[i+1].base == frames[i].base + frames[i].closure.proto.num_registers. A non-empty vararg range lies below its frame base inside the live stack prefix; an empty range is encoded as base/count zero. The bottom (main) frame leaves ret_dest/ret_count unused.

LoadedChunk.description: One runtime-`load`ed chunk's recompile inputs (L-2): its source text and the chunk name it was loaded under. Restore re-parses + re-compiles `source` (compile is deterministic) and renames the root proto to `name`, so a live `load` closure — and any post-restore fault it raises — is byte-identical to the pre-snapshot VM.

Keyframe.description: A whole-VM state snapshot at one moment (docs/design/04-snapshot-replay-schema.md). The heap is a flat array of objects keyed by id; roots are the globals table id, the shared string-metatable id (1-based optional id: header.id + 1, or 0 = none), the live register window, the active frame closures, and the open upvalues. F2a captures the final state (empty stack/frames/open_upvalues); F2b adds mid-execution capture. `next_obj_id` is the heap's monotonic allocation counter (the next `GcHeader.id` to hand out): serialized so restore reproduces the id timeline EXACTLY even when objects were allocated-then-dropped before the cut (pre-cut garbage bumps the counter but leaves no object in `objects`, so reconstructing the counter as max(id)+1 would drift it low and diverge subsequent ids — which are observable via table/pairs ordering). `loaded_chunks` (L-2) carries every runtime-`load`ed chunk's source + name in load order: restore RE-COMPILES each (compile is deterministic) to regenerate identical protos/ids, so a live `load` closure survives snapshot→restore without serializing bytecode.

SnapshotFile.description: The top-level keyframe artifact. Versioned independently of TraceFile (its own `version` word) — a distinct record family sharing the same binschema encoding, NOT fused with the trace artifact (docs/design/04: 'two artifacts, one substrate').

EffectResult.description: An effect's recorded result. Its OWN tag space (deliberately NOT a Value.Tag mirror like SnapValue): scalars plus an inline string, never a heap_ref. A standalone effect log has no idmap, so a string result (getenv/argv) is carried as inline length-prefixed bytes (ConstString) and re-interned on replay; tables/closures are never effect results. tag: nil=0, bool=1, int=2, float=3, string=4.

Effect.description: One recorded nondeterministic INPUT: the host effect that produced it and the Value it returned. `kind` mirrors mahina's interp.EffectKind enum (clock=0, random_seed=1, getenv=2, argc=3, argv=4). The log is consumed in call order on replay; kind + result fully describe each entry (effect args are re-supplied by re-executing the same instruction stream). `result` is an EffectResult — scalars (clock/argc/random_seed) plus inline string bytes (getenv/argv), never a heap_ref.

EffectFile.description: The top-level effect-log artifact (F2d): the ordered list of recorded nondeterministic inputs for one run. Its own `version` word — a third record family sharing the binschema encoding with the trace and keyframe artifacts, never fused (docs/design/04 'two artifacts, one substrate'). Replay restores a keyframe and feeds these back in order so re-execution past an effect is reproducible.

ExecEvent.description: One event in a trace entry's execution stream (the viz iteration animation). `kind`: value=0 (a non-guard IR instruction produced `value`; `ref` = its SSA index), guard_pass=1 (a guard survived; `value` = the checked operand), commit=2 (a loop back-edge closed; `ref`/`value` unused), exit=3 (the entry side-exited at IR `ref`; terminal; `value` = the failing guard's operand or nil for an arith error). `value` reuses EffectResult — trace values are scalars at this phase (no heap/table IR ops; those abort tracing), so the self-contained scalar-or-inline-string encoding fits exactly.

TraceEntry.description: One trace entry = one IR-interpreter execute() call (an 'exit ramp'): the iterations it spun and the side-exit that ended it. `iterations` is the executor's yield (accurate even when `capped`). `exit_ref` = the faulting IR instruction; `exit_kind`: guard=0 / arith=1 / clean=2. `capped` = the per-entry `events` detail was truncated at the iteration cap (the terminal `exit` event is still present).

TraceExecLog.description: All recorded entries (exit ramps) for one cached trace, keyed by `trace_id` — the trace's stable `Trace.id`, matching `Trace.id` in the trace file (a retired trace's log is dropped with it). `entries_capped` = the entry cap was hit and further entries were not recorded.

ExecLogFile.description: The top-level trace execution-log artifact (the JIT-trace iteration animation): per-trace execution logs for one run. Its own `version` word — a FOURTH record family sharing the binschema encoding with the trace/keyframe/effect artifacts, never fused (docs/design/04 'two artifacts, one substrate', now four). Unlike the effect log it is an *observation* log, not a replay input — nothing feeds it back; the visualizer animates it.

JitCounters.description: The raw JIT event counters (TraceState, src/trace.zig), mirroring the '--jit-stats' event-counter block. Always live regardless of the coverage gate — they cost nothing on the hot path. link arm/fuse/disarm track the native chaining machinery; the *link_exits/*follow* pairs count exit-chaining hops; prime_side_* the coherent-state-chaining source arming.

CoverageAnchor.description: Per-loop-header JIT execution coverage (AnchorCoverage, src/trace.zig), keyed by the anchor's stable proto id (never the *const Proto pointer) plus loop-header pc. `traced_iters`/`interp_iters` are back-edge counts (ran-as-trace vs fell-back-to-tier-0); `traced_cycles`/`interp_cycles` are the per-hop TSC attribution (0 on a target without rdtsc). `has_trace` = a compiled trace exists at this anchor — so an anchor with has_trace=1 and traced_iters=0 is the smell: it has a trace but ran fully interpreted.

CoverageFile.description: The top-level JIT-coverage artifact (Phase 2): the aggregate native-vs-tier-0 execution split by iterations AND by TSC time, the raw event counters, and the per-anchor breakdown. Its own `version` word — a FIFTH record family sharing the binschema encoding, never fused (docs/design/04 'two artifacts, one substrate'). An *observation* artifact, not a replay input. `cycles_*`/`run_cycles` are 0 on a target without rdtsc (the wasm VM), in which case the visualizer shows time as n/a and weighs by iterations only. `anchors` is sorted (proto_id, pc) for a reproducible artifact.
